name: hyperbolic_geometry
description: Hyperbolic geometry -- reuses Euclidean layers 0-3 (absolute geometry), replaces the parallel axiom with the hyperbolic parallel postulate (Lobachevsky form)
author: Lv-00 Core Team

layers.name: incidence
layers.note: Incidence axioms are identical in hyperbolic geometry. Points and lines satisfy the same basic relations.

layers.name: order
layers.note: Betweenness axioms are identical. The concept of 'between' is unchanged in hyperbolic geometry.

layers.name: congruence
layers.note: Segment congruence axioms are identical. Absolute geometry is preserved up to this layer.

layers.name: continuity
layers.note: Continuity axiom is the same. Both Euclidean and hyperbolic lines are Dedekind-complete.

layers.name: hyperbolic_parallel
layers.description: Hyperbolic parallel postulate -- replaces Playfair. Through a point not on a line, there exist INFINITELY MANY lines parallel to the given line.

axioms.name: Hyperbolic Parallel Postulate
axioms.signature: forall (A : Point) (l : Line), ~on(A, l) -> exists (m1 m2 : Line), on(A, m1) /\ on(A, m2) /\ m1 != m2 /\ ~intersect(l, m1) /\ ~intersect(l, m2)
axioms.note: This axiom asserts the existence of AT LEAST TWO parallels through a point. Combined with the properties of absolute geometry, this implies INFINITELY MANY parallels.

layers.independence_notes: The hyperbolic parallel postulate is the negation of Playfair. It is consistent with layers 0-3 (Beltrami-Klein and Poincare disk models prove relative consistency).

models.name: Poincare Disk Model
models.description: Points are interior of unit disk; lines are circular arcs orthogonal to boundary

models.name: Beltrami-Klein Model
models.description: Points are interior of unit disk; lines are Euclidean chords

models.name: Hyperboloid Model
models.description: Points on upper sheet of two-sheeted hyperboloid in Minkowski space

parallel_postulate.euclidean: Exactly ONE parallel through a point not on a line
parallel_postulate.hyperbolic: INFINITELY MANY parallels through a point not on a line

theorems_that_change.hyperbolic: Similar triangles are necessarily congruent (AAA is a congruence criterion)

theorems_that_change.euclidean: Rectangles (quadrilaterals with four right angles) exist
theorems_that_change.hyperbolic: No rectangles exist (Saccheri-Legendre: at most 3 right angles)

theorems_that_change.euclidean: Distance between parallel lines is constant
theorems_that_change.hyperbolic: Distance between parallel lines varies (approaches 0 in one direction, infinity in the other)
Area = pi - (alpha + beta + gamma), where alpha, beta, gamma are angles in radians (Gauss-Bonnet)

theorems_that_stay_the_same: All theorems of absolute geometry (layers 0-3 alone) -- e.g., Saccheri-Legendre theorem, exterior angle theorem, triangle congruence criteria (SAS, ASA, SSS)

references: Lobachevsky, N.I. 'Geometrical Researches on the Theory of Parallels' (1840).
Bolyai, J. 'Appendix Scientiam Spatii Absolute Veram Exhibens' (1832).
Beltrami, E. 'Saggio di interpretazione della geometria non-euclidea' (1868). Giornale di Matematiche.
Poincare, H. 'Theorie des groupes fuchsiens' (1882). Acta Mathematica.
Anderson, J.W. 'Hyperbolic Geometry' (2nd ed., 2005). Springer Undergraduate Mathematics Series.
